department: Faculty of Science — Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences

deadline.value: Main Round and Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme (HKPFS) deadline for 2027-28 entry is December 1, 2026 (1st Clearing Round: April 30, 2027; 2nd Clearing Round: August 31, 2027).

also.quote: In view of the limited admission quota, applicants are strongly encouraged to apply in the Main Round. Applications will be considered in the clearing rounds only if there are vacancies after the Main Round.

gre_subject.value: No ETS GRE Subject Test exists for earth and planetary sciences (ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics, and Psychology).
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences states it is essential for prospective students to contact potential supervisors ahead of application submission to discuss project details and confirm availability.
supervisor.quote: It is essential for prospective students to contact potential supervisor(s) ahead of application submission in order to determine if he/she/they are interested in admitting a new student and to discuss project details.

funding.value: Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences guarantees full financial support during study for formally registered research students.
funding.quote: A formally registered research student will have full financial support during his/her study at the University of Hong Kong.

entry_route.value: Admits good honours bachelor's and/or taught master's holders to the 4-year PhD, and research master's (e.g., MPhil) holders to the 3-year PhD.
entry_route.quote: The University offers 3-year and 4-year PhD programmes. Applicants who have a good Bachelor’s degree with honours and/or a taught Master’s degree will be considered for admission to a 4-year PhD programme, whereas those who already hold a research Master’s degree (e.g. MPhil) will only be considered for admission to a 3-year PhD programme.

notes: Applications require a research proposal; full financial support guaranteed for registered research students.
